transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Um, well... I guess I'm here because of elevators. I know they aren't actually dangerous or anything, but... I don't know. When I have to get in one, I just get really scared, like I'm going to get trapped in there. And I just can't seem to make myself feel normal about it.
Are there other situations or places where you feel similar anxiety, such as crowded spaces, open areas, or being outside your home?
Um, no. Not really. Just... just the elevators. Being outside or in crowds is fine. It's really just that one thing.
When you're in an elevator, do you ever experience sudden physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shortness of breath?

Yeah, I do. Um... as soon as those doors start sliding shut, my chest gets kind of tight. And my hands get sweaty. I just... all I can think is that I need out. Even if I'm only going up, like, a few floors.
Have you ever had a panic attack or felt like you were about to have one while in an elevator?
Um... I don't really know. Not really, I guess. I just get worked up, like I said. I don't think it's an actual attack or anything... I just don't like being in them.
Do you find yourself avoiding elevators altogether or doing anything differently in your daily routine to prevent having to use one?

Um, yeah. I guess so. I mean, most days I just take the stairs. At my apartment, or... or on job sites. If I have to use an elevator or a lift to get up high, I usually just ask if there's something else I can do instead. If I absolutely have to ride it, I'll only do it if someone I know and trust is right there with me. Otherwise, I just... I don't.
